To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thin BOX SOI technology is capable of achieving high energy capabilities and high BVdss for both high side and low side LDMOS transis-tors.
the power LDMOS devices in thin BOX SOIs have comparable breakdown voltage, energy handling capability, and robust performance as bulk BCD technologies.
the thin BOX SOI technology enables a new class of power LDMOS with high energy capability and state of the art trade-off between Rdson and BVdss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of power LDMOS devices for high energy applications.
the design and optimization of power LDMOS for thin BOX SOI.
the design, process, and characterization of thin BOX SOI LDMOS transis-tors for power ICs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thin BOX SOI power LDMOS devices can be successfully implemented in BCD processes with high energy capability and robust breakdown voltage performance.
the thin BOX SOI technology is capable of providing high energy capability and state-of-the-art Rdson/BVddss trade-off for power NLDMOS devices.
the power LDMOS devices built in thin BOX SOIs can achieve high energy capability, comparable to bulk BDC technologies and almost identical BVdss for both high and lower side applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thin BOX SOI technology is an excellent candidate for the integration of high voltage power devices with high energy capabilities.
the thin BOX SOI technology is a viable alternative to the bulk BCD technology for the high energy power LDMOS application.
thin BOX SOI power LDMOS devices can be built with state of the arts Rdson and BVdss, and the performance can be further optimized by proper device design and process optimization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thin BOX SOI power devices are not necessarily inferior to bulk BCD power devices in terms of breakdown voltage, energy capability, or robustness.
the BOX SOI platform can be used as an alternative to bulk BCD for high voltage power LDMOS design.
the thin BOX SOI process can be used for high voltage applications, and the high energy capability of the thin BOX SOIs can be further exploited by the proper design of the device structures.
